qualified_claim: Desktop installation approval and credential-restoring recovery now share the existing per-radio setup admission with Remote Access provisioning. Qualification covers cooperating same-UID Linux processes sharing the lock namespace, including actual OS-keychain completion after model retirement.
before: The new injected regression failed against the unchanged approve() implementation from base 522d482fa: approval proceeded while another setup held admission. The baseline only added an unused private injection seam and the regression; it did not change approve() behavior.

implementation.approval: Acquire nonblocking per-radio admission before the first attempt credential save or upgrade credential load. Refusal preserves the reviewed plan and permits an explicit retry without new credentials, journal changes, upload or automatic retry.
implementation.lifetime: Retain model admission through the running coordinator, public cleanup and active-credential promotion. Read-only saved recovery acquires it before observing a result that may restore the active credential; saved-package preparation does not hold it across human approval.
implementation.pending_writes: A shared completion hold outlives cancellation, deadline or model destruction until the default credential backend finishes. Callback copies consume one shared hold so retaining or duplicating an acknowledged completion cannot lock out future jobs or release a newer job.
implementation.terminal_paths: Release the model hold on finished, failed or canceled local phases. An already-started credential write independently retains admission through its actual backend outcome.
implementation.provider_contract: TokenWriter providers run on the model thread and must retain the completion object until their backend outcome; a dead context suppresses delivery, not job ownership. The default TailnetShimTokenStore provider is exercised with actual OS-keychain jobs.
implementation.operator_status: Existing installation status reports busy/unavailable admission and keeps approval available for explicit retry. No new widget, modal prompt, thread, signal route, dependency, endpoint or on-radio privilege.
